name: nlp_sentence_embedding
title: A sentence encoder trained on paraphrase pairs with a scaled-cosine head and a Spearman validation pass
origin: hardening round 1, domain-nlp, 2026-09-13 - the embedding/contrastive shape
note: MLV301, MLV302 and MLV501 fire only under --dataflow ip. MLV402 misses in both modes: the value handed to nn.BCELoss comes from torch.cosine_similarity * a scale tensor, which is neither a sigmoid nor a recognised logits producer, so the final-op chain walk has nothing to type.

expected.why: the validation pairs change on every run, so the Spearman correlation this script reports cannot be compared with yesterday's
paraphrase corpora are stored with the positive pairs grouped by source, so every batch is one topic and the in-batch contrast the loss depends on is between near-duplicates

expected.defect: a four-worker DataLoader is constructed at module scope with no if __name__ == "__main__" guard
expected.why: on Windows and macOS the worker processes re-import the module, re-run build_splits() and re-enter the loader construction, which either deadlocks or forks the whole corpus load four times

expected.defect: nn.BCELoss is fed a cosine similarity scaled by 20, which lives in [-20, 20]
expected.why: BCELoss requires its input in [0, 1]; every negative similarity makes log(x) undefined, so the loss is NaN from the first batch that contains a dissimilar pair and the run silently stops learning

expected.defect: the running loss accumulates the tensor rather than loss.item()
expected.why: five epochs of autograd graphs are kept alive at once, which is an out-of-memory on the third epoch and nothing else

expected.defect: the model is moved to the device but none of the four batch tensors is
expected.why: a CPU tensor fed to a moved module raises at run time as soon as device is anything but cpu
the transformer encoder keeps its dropout active, so the validation correlation is measured on a randomly perturbed encoder

expected.defect: the Spearman pass is not wrapped in torch.no_grad()
expected.why: the whole validation split's autograd graph is built and discarded
the split, the initialisation and the dropout masks all move between runs

forbidden.why: optimizer.zero_grad() is the first statement of the batch loop (line 48)
optimizer.step() is called on line 52, after the backward on line 51
there is no torch.no_grad() block in this project, so no backward can be inside one
the validation loader passes shuffle=False explicitly (line 37)
there is no softmax and no CrossEntropyLoss anywhere in this project
the encoder layers are held by nn.TransformerEncoder, which registers them; no plain list or dict of modules is assigned to self
nothing is fitted before random_split - the archive is already vectorised token ids
the only metric is a rank correlation over continuous similarities, which is what spearmanr takes

unsupported.defect: the temperature is allocated on the default device inside forward(), so on CUDA it is a CPU scalar multiplied into a CUDA tensor on every forward
unsupported.why: MLV503 (tensor allocated inside a batch loop with no device=) is a later-tier rule and is not built

unsupported.defect: the padding mask is passed to the encoder as `attention_mask == 0` and to mean_pool as the raw mask, so the two halves of the pooling use opposite conventions if a caller ever passes an inverted mask
the split is executed at import time, so every worker process re-runs it and - with no generator - gets a different split than the parent
unsupported.why: no rule relates module-scope execution to DataLoader worker re-import; MLV112 covers the guard itself, not what the missing guard re-executes
